rootCauseAnalysis.summary: payment-service-pdb allows zero voluntary disruptions because minAvailable: 2 equals the two healthy payment-service replicas; this is a configuration/capacity condition, not pod failure.
causalChain: Signal: `KubePodDisruptionBudgetAtLimit` reports `payment-service-pdb` with zero allowed voluntary disruptions.
Why? The PDB has `minAvailable: 2`, while its selector currently matches exactly `2` healthy/expected pods; therefore `2 - 2 = 0` disruptions are allowed.
Why are there only two matched pods? Deployment `payment-service` and ReplicaSet `payment-service-7f7f779d` are configured and observed at `2` replicas.
Why does that configuration produce maintenance sensitivity? The workload has no spare replica beyond the PDB's minimum availability requirement, so evicting either pod would violate the budget.

Root cause: `payment-service` is configured with only `2` replicas while `payment-service-pdb` requires `minAvailable: 2`; the workload/PDB sizing combination intentionally leaves zero voluntary-disruption headroom.
